authority.contract: A zero-length span is a real insertion point; null means unknown. Parser insertion diagnostics use a known zero-length span only when the insertion location is known.
Diagnostics with TABLE origin should point to modifier or column text; diagnostics without table-origin metadata use the normal empty-span fallback while retaining the datasource message.

observedConflict.currentReporterBehavior: SourceContractDiagnosticReporter.ResolveSpan returns TextSpan.Empty when no source-context location exists, then DiagnosticContext maps that empty span through SourceText.GetLocations.
observedConflict.currentEnvelopeEffect: A provider diagnostic with no table-origin metadata is emitted as a known offset-zero query location, conflating unavailable location with a real insertion.
observedConflict.preservedControl: A caller that explicitly supplies DiagnosticContext.ReportWarning(..., TextSpan.Empty) continues to receive a known zero-length insertion.

resolution.decision: Interpret the table specification's empty-span fallback as unavailable location at the diagnostic envelope boundary when no table-origin mapping exists.
rationale: The core diagnostic contract makes null and known zero-length locations semantically distinct.
SourceContractDiagnosticReporter can distinguish absent mapping from an explicitly mapped span by returning nullable TextSpan.
The direct DiagnosticContext TextSpan API remains unchanged, so intentional zero-length insertions are not weakened.
resolution.implementationBoundary: SourceContractDiagnosticReporter uses no-span DiagnosticContext overloads only when ResolveSpan has no mapped modifier or column span.
resolution.evidence: REC-126 D01, D02, D05 and D06 permanent tests; initial pre-fix TRX is preserved under .campaign-artifacts/REC-126-focused-initial.
